interactions.label: A 9-year-old has point tenderness over the proximal tibial metaphysis with warmt

params.question: A 9-year-old has point tenderness over the proximal tibial metaphysis with warmth and swelling. Passive knee movement causes mild discomfort but is far less painful than direct palpation of the bone. What does this pattern suggest?

answers.text: Septic arthritis of the knee, because any pain on joint movement indicates joint infection

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. In septic arthritis, movement in every direction is exquisitely painful. When tenderness is worst over the metaphysis with relatively preserved joint movement, the infection is more likely in the bone, not the joint.

answers.text: Acute osteomyelitis, because metaphyseal tenderness exceeding joint pain is the key early sign

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In early osteomyelitis the infection lies in the metaphysis, not the joint. Point tenderness over the metaphysis with relatively preserved joint movement is the key examination finding distinguishing it from septic arthritis, where all directions of joint movement are painful.

answers.text: A soft tissue abscess, because localised swelling is the dominant finding

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A soft tissue abscess is superficial and fluctuant, without the deep metaphyseal tenderness characteristic of bone infection. The combination of fever, metaphyseal tenderness, and swelling points to osteomyelitis.

answers.text: A pathological fracture, because point tenderness over bone indicates cortical disruption

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While fractures cause point tenderness, the clinical context — fever, warmth, metaphyseal location, and no history of trauma — points to infection, not injury.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key distinction: in osteomyelitis, tenderness is maximal over the metaphysis with relatively preserved joint movement. In septic arthritis, every direction of joint movement causes severe pain.

Well done. In osteomyelitis, tenderness is maximal at the metaphysis with relatively preserved joint movement. In septic arthritis, movement in every direction is exquisitely painful — that is the key bedside distinction.

interactions.label: A 28-year-old presents with progressive knee swelling over four months, low-grad

params.question: A 28-year-old presents with progressive knee swelling over four months, low-grade evening fever, and weight loss. ESR is mildly elevated but CRP is near-normal. Which feature most strongly suggests a tuberculous rather than pyogenic aetiology?

answers.text: Involvement of the knee joint

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Both pyogenic and tuberculous infections can involve the knee. The specific joint affected does not reliably distinguish between the two aetiologies.

answers.text: Elevated ESR

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ESR is elevated in both pyogenic and tuberculous infections. It is a general marker of inflammation and is not specific to either cause.

answers.text: Insidious onset over months with predominantly constitutional symptoms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Tempo is the key discriminator. Pyogenic infection presents acutely over days with high fever and markedly raised inflammatory markers, whereas tuberculosis evolves insidiously over months with low-grade constitutional symptoms and only mildly elevated markers.

answers.text: Male sex of the patient

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Sex alone does not distinguish pyogenic from tuberculous musculoskeletal infection. The clinical tempo and pattern of systemic features are the key differentiators.

overallFeedback.feedback: Tempo is the key discriminator. Pyogenic infection is acute (days, high fever, markedly raised CRP), while tuberculosis is insidious (months, low-grade fever, weight loss, mildly raised markers). Misdiagnosis in either direction delays correct treatment.

Excellent. The insidious course with constitutional symptoms and mildly raised markers points to TB. Pyogenic infection would present acutely over days with high fever and a CRP surge. Getting this distinction wrong in either direction causes real harm.

interactions.label: A normal plain radiograph in the first week of symptoms reliably excludes a diag

params.question: A normal plain radiograph in the first week of symptoms reliably excludes a diagnosis of acute osteomyelitis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Plain radiographs are often normal in the first 7–10 days because bone must lose 30–50% of its mineral content before destruction appears. A normal X-ray does not rule out early osteomyelitis — MRI is far more sensitive in this window.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Plain radiographs are often normal in the first 7–10 days because bone must lose 30–50% of its mineral content before lytic changes become visible. MRI is the gold standard for early detection, showing bone marrow oedema within days of onset.

interactions.label: During aspiration of a febrile patient's hot, swollen knee, you obtain turbid sy

params.question: During aspiration of a febrile patient's hot, swollen knee, you obtain turbid synovial fluid. The laboratory reports a white cell count of 82,000/μL with 94% neutrophils and a synovial glucose less than half the serum level. What is the most appropriate interpretation?

answers.text: Inflammatory arthritis requiring elective rheumatology referral

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While inflammatory arthritis raises the white cell count, counts above 50,000/μL with >90% neutrophils and low glucose cross the threshold for presumptive septic arthritis, which is an emergency — not an elective referral.

answers.text: Presumptive septic arthritis requiring urgent treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Turbid fluid with >50,000 white cells/μL, >90% neutrophils, and glucose less than half the serum level is the standard threshold for presumptive septic arthritis. In a febrile patient, this mandates urgent antibiotics and surgical drainage.

answers.text: Crystal arthropathy such as gout, based on the turbidity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Gout can produce turbid fluid, but diagnosis requires identification of monosodium urate crystals under polarised light microscopy. This combination of very high white cell count, neutrophil predominance, and low glucose in a febrile patient strongly indicates septic arthritis.

answers.text: Normal post-traumatic effusion with reactive changes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Post-traumatic effusions are typically haemorrhagic or only mildly elevated in cell count, not turbid with >80,000 white cells and neutrophil predominance. This pattern indicates infection, not injury.

overallFeedback.feedback: Turbid fluid with >50,000 WCC, >90% neutrophils, and low glucose in a febrile patient is presumptive septic arthritis — an orthopaedic emergency requiring urgent antibiotics and joint drainage.

Well done. The classic septic profile — >50,000 WCC, >90% neutrophils, and low glucose — in a febrile patient demands urgent treatment. Even borderline counts (25,000–50,000) in a febrile patient should be treated as septic until proven otherwise.

interactions.label: A patient with acute osteomyelitis fails to improve after 48 hours of appropriat

params.question: A patient with acute osteomyelitis fails to improve after 48 hours of appropriate intravenous antibiotics. What is the primary reason surgical intervention is now indicated?

answers.text: Antibiotics are intrinsically ineffective against bone infections

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Antibiotics are effective against bone infections when the tissue has adequate blood supply. The problem arises only when infection creates avascular zones or walled-off collections that antibiotics cannot penetrate.

answers.text: Antibiotics cannot penetrate avascular or walled-off tissue collections

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This is the key principle: once infection creates an abscess or devitalised bone, antibiotics cannot cross the avascular barrier. Surgery drains collections and removes dead tissue, restoring a field where antibiotics can work.

answers.text: Surgical debridement alone cures osteomyelitis without the need for antibiotics

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Surgery and antibiotics work together. Surgery removes barriers to antibiotic penetration, while antibiotics clear residual bacteria. Neither alone is sufficient when an abscess has formed.

answers.text: Two days is always too short for antibiotics to show any clinical effect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Appropriate antibiotics should produce clinical improvement — reduced fever, decreasing pain — within 36–48 hours. Failure to improve in this window is a warning that a collection has formed, requiring surgical drainage.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key principle: antibiotics cannot penetrate avascular or walled-off tissue. Failure to improve after 36–48 hours of appropriate antibiotics suggests an abscess or devitalised bone that requires surgical drainage.

Exactly right. The guiding principle is that antibiotics cannot reach avascular or walled-off tissue. Failure to improve after 36–48 hours suggests an undrained abscess or dead bone acting as a barrier to treatment.

interactions.label: On post-operative day 1 following arthrotomy for hip septic arthritis, the surgi

params.question: On post-operative day 1 following arthrotomy for hip septic arthritis, the surgical drain output drops suddenly from 50 mL to zero, but the wound appears swollen and tense. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Successful drainage with complete resolution of the effusion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. If drainage were complete, you would not expect increasing wound swelling and tension. A sudden drop in output combined with wound swelling indicates fluid accumulation that cannot exit — not resolution.

answers.text: Drain occlusion by fibrin clot

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Fibrin occlusion of the drain is a common early post-operative complication. Sudden cessation of output combined with wound swelling means fluid is accumulating but cannot exit. Prompt recognition and drain flushing or replacement prevents secondary infection.

answers.text: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Avascular necrosis is a late complication developing weeks to months after septic arthritis from sustained pressure compromising the femoral head blood supply. It does not present as wound swelling on post-operative day 1.

answers.text: Deep vein thrombosis of the lower limb

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Deep vein thrombosis typically presents with diffuse calf swelling, pain, and tenderness — not localised wound swelling with cessation of drain output. The pattern here points to a mechanical drain problem.

overallFeedback.feedback: A sudden drop in drain output with wound swelling and tension on post-operative day 1 indicates drain occlusion by fibrin. Early recognition prevents the drained wound from becoming a closed pus collection again.

Correct. Sudden cessation of drain output with wound swelling on day 1 is fibrin occlusion until proven otherwise. This is one of three early complications to watch for — alongside wound haematoma and neurovascular compromise.
